title: Serious illness conversation template and prompts on medical and oncology wards: what to test first
subtitle: Evaluation design not yet settled
statement: Only 22 of 120 patients who died in the hospital last year had a documented goals-of-care conversation before the last week of life, and most notes recorded only resuscitation status. The hospital plans a serious illness conversation template with prognostic prompts and a short skills session on six medical and oncology wards from February 2027. It is not yet clear whether to evaluate this with a stepped-wedge randomised design or a chart review before and after, or whether documentation is even the right outcome, because published results conflict on whether templates improve what is written.
whoAffected: Adults with serious illness admitted to the medical and oncology wards, their families, ward doctors and nurses, and the palliative care consult team.
whatHurts: Patients reach the last week of life without their goals known; families are left to guess; notes that record only resuscitation status give a false impression that planning happened.
currentPractice: A free-text advance care planning note, completed inconsistently; conversations mostly happen late or not at all.
whyNow: The template is scheduled for the February 2027 release, a small internal grant is available, and the research office wants an evaluation plan.
constraints: Internal grant of 15,000 for one year. Data analyst available 6 hours per month. Ward staff can attend at most one 60-minute training session each. The template can only go live in the record build team's February 2027 release.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients with serious illness have a timely conversation about what matters to them, recorded in a way that shapes their care.
summary: Problem framed; the design family is left unresolved (randomised or chart review) until the evidence is reviewed.
